action_criteria.expected_evidence: Right frontal 5.8 cm mass in the superior and middle frontal gyri reaching the precentral gyrus and corpus callosum, with thick irregular ring enhancement, central necrosis, rim restricted diffusion, edema into the posterior limb of the internal capsule and 8 mm leftward midline shift
action_criteria.label: Order MRI brain with and without gadolinium contrast (tumor protocol with DWI, FLAIR, post-contrast T1) to characterize the right frontal lesion, define mass effect, and plan surgery
action_criteria.rationale: Contrast MRI with diffusion and FLAIR characterizes the lesion and its mass effect, identifies the enhancing target and plans the surgical approach (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Maximum rCBV ratio 5.8 in the enhancing rim with a low-perfusion necrotic cavity, supporting a high-grade neoplasm and targeting sampling
action_criteria.label: Order MR perfusion imaging (DSC perfusion) to assess tumor vascularity and target highest-grade region for biopsy
action_criteria.rationale: Perfusion supports a high-grade neoplasm and identifies the most vascular region to sample; tissue decides the diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Cho/NAA 6.8 with lipid-lactate in the enhancing component and raised choline in the peritumoral FLAIR region
action_criteria.label: Order MR spectroscopy (1H-MRS) to characterize tumor metabolic profile
action_criteria.rationale: Spectroscopy supports a high-grade neoplasm and shows infiltration beyond the enhancing margin; tissue decides the diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No extracranial primary malignancy identified, supporting primary brain tumor as the working diagnosis
action_criteria.label: Order CT chest/abdomen/pelvis as staging to exclude an extracranial primary if a solitary metastasis is on the differential
action_criteria.rationale: A former smoker with a family history of lung and colon cancer: staging CT excludes an extracranial primary if a solitary metastasis is considered.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Glucose 142 mg/dL and HbA1c 6.7% in known type 2 diabetes, relevant to dexamethasone; electrolytes, platelets and coagulation normal: no laboratory contraindication to surgery
action_criteria.label: Order pre-operative laboratory workup: CBC, comprehensive metabolic panel, coagulation studies (PT/INR, aPTT), and type & screen in anticipation of surgical biopsy/resection
action_criteria.rationale: Surgery and corticosteroids are planned; coagulation, platelets, electrolytes, glucose and a group and screen are needed first.

action_criteria.label: Score performance status (Karnofsky and ECOG) at this visit
action_criteria.rationale: The choice between standard and hypofractionated chemoradiotherapy depends on age and Karnofsky performance status (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Left-hand motor activation displaced posteriorly about 8 mm from the enhancing margin; left-hemisphere language dominance (laterality index 0.85)
action_criteria.label: Order functional MRI (motor and language mapping) before resection of the right frontal tumor reaching the precentral gyrus
action_criteria.rationale: The tumor extends to the right precentral gyrus; motor and language mapping defines the resection margin (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Right corticospinal tract displaced and continuous through the edematous corona radiata, about 9 mm from the enhancing margin
action_criteria.label: Order DTI tractography of the right corticospinal tract before resection
action_criteria.rationale: The edema extends through the corona radiata into the posterior limb of the internal capsule; tractography locates the corticospinal tract (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Integrated diagnosis Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4 with IDH1 R132H negative and IDH1/IDH2 wildtype on sequencing, ATRX retained, MGMT promoter unmethylated
action_criteria.label: Obtain tissue by maximal safe resection of the right frontal lesion, or stereotactic biopsy if resection is not safely feasible, for an integrated histomolecular diagnosis with IDH1 R132H immunohistochemistry, IDH1/IDH2 sequencing (age under 55), ATRX immunohistochemistry and MGMT promoter methylation
action_criteria.rationale: Surgery is the first option for a resectable glioma and should be as extensive as safely possible (AIOM; EANO 2021). Only tissue establishes the integrated diagnosis and the molecular results that select treatment.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Steroid hyperglycemia on metformin identified; levetiracetam free of relevant interactions
action_criteria.label: Check interactions of dexamethasone and levetiracetam, started in the emergency department, with the current medicines (metformin, amlodipine, lisinopril, atorvastatin, tamsulosin)
action_criteria.rationale: Dexamethasone worsens glycemic control on metformin; enzyme-inducing antiseizure drugs are avoided.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not perform lumbar puncture: the 8 mm midline shift and bilateral papilledema create a risk of herniation.
Do not initiate definitive tumor-directed therapy (radiation, temozolomide, alkylating chemotherapy) before tissue diagnosis is established
Do not start therapeutic anticoagulation without a clear thromboembolic indication, given upcoming neurosurgical intervention and bleeding risk
required_recommendations: Refer urgently to neurosurgery for maximal safe resection of the right frontal lesion, with preoperative functional MRI and DTI tractography and intraoperative mapping, with stereotactic biopsy if resection is not safely feasible; send the specimen for an integrated histomolecular diagnosis (WHO CNS5).
Continue dexamethasone, started in the emergency department, for symptomatic vasogenic edema at the lowest effective dose, with glucose monitoring and gastric protection, and taper after surgery.

Continue levetiracetam, started in the emergency department, for the documented focal seizure with left arm onset, leftward head and eye version and bilateral tonic-clonic spread, and review the dose for renal function and seizure control; this is treatment of tumor-related epilepsy, not prophylaxis. Avoid enzyme-inducing antiseizure drugs (phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital), which lower dexamethasone and chemotherapy exposure.
Record the latex allergy (contact dermatitis) for a latex-safe operating theatre and ward.
Monitor capillary glucose at least every 6 hours on dexamethasone and adjust the antihyperglycemic regimen (metformin, adding insulin if needed), given type 2 diabetes.

After the integrated diagnosis, refer to the neuro-oncology multidisciplinary team; for glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype at age 70 or under with KPS 70 or more, radiotherapy 60 Gy in 30 fractions with concomitant and adjuvant temozolomide (Stupp 2005; EANO 2021).

differential.key_features: Former smoker with family history of lung and colon cancer, but no known primary; staging CT chest, abdomen and pelvis negative; a single infiltrative mass reaching the corpus callosum favors a primary glioma; tissue shows a glial neoplasm
Age 52 keeps it in consideration until IDH is known; IDH1 R132H negative, IDH1/IDH2 wildtype on sequencing and ATRX retained exclude it
Immunocompetent; thick irregular ring enhancement with central necrosis rather than homogeneous enhancement with diffuse restriction; tissue shows a glial neoplasm
Afebrile, WBC 8.7, CRP 3.1 mg/L; restricted diffusion at the enhancing rim rather than the core and rCBV 5.8 in the rim argue against pus
Closed thick ring with nodular enhancement, central necrosis and marked mass effect are atypical; demyelination usually shows an open ring and low rCBV

key_clinical_evidence: Weeks of morning headache with vomiting, left arm weakness and a first focal seizure with leftward version and bilateral spread call for urgent contrast-enhanced brain MRI

The MRI shows a right frontal mass reaching the precentral gyrus and corpus callosum with thick irregular ring enhancement, central necrosis, rim restricted diffusion and 8 mm midline shift: a high-grade neoplasm on imaging
Perfusion (rCBV 5.8) and spectroscopy (Cho/NAA 6.8, lipid-lactate) support a high-grade neoplasm and target sampling; they do not grade the tumor
Bilateral papilledema and 8 mm midline shift: dexamethasone continues, and lumbar puncture is contraindicated

Only tissue gives the integrated diagnosis: at 52, IDH1 R132H IHC negative is confirmed by IDH1/IDH2 sequencing; with ATRX retained, microvascular proliferation and necrosis it is glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4; MGMT is unmethylated

The tumor reaches the precentral gyrus and its edema involves the corticospinal tract, so functional MRI and DTI plan a maximal safe resection; at 52 with KPS 70 the standard after surgery is the Stupp regimen
Levetiracetam started in the emergency department continues as treatment of tumor-related epilepsy, not prophylaxis; enzyme-inducing drugs are avoided because of dexamethasone and temozolomide
The latex allergy must be flagged before surgery

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Diego Ramirez is a 52-year-old right-handed man with a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia who presents to the emergency department after a witnessed generalized tonic-clonic seizure at home this morning. His wife reports that over the past three to four weeks, he has been complaining of progressively worsening headaches, predominantly on the right side, that are worst in the early morning and sometimes wake him from sleep. She notes that the headaches are unlike any he has experienced before and are associated with nausea and occasional vomiting. Over the past two weeks, she has also noticed that he has been clumsier with his left hand, dropping things more frequently, and that his left arm seems weaker than usual. He has also become slower to respond in conversations, which is very uncharacteristic for him as a school principal. His colleagues at work have remarked that he seems less organized and occasionally forgetful over the past month. This morning at approximately 7:15 AM, while eating breakfast, he suddenly stopped speaking, his eyes and head turned to the left, and he developed rhythmic jerking of the left arm that rapidly generalized to a full tonic-clonic convulsion lasting approximately 90 seconds. He was postictal and confused for about 20 minutes before EMS arrived. He had never had a seizure before. In the emergency department, a non-contrast CT of the head was obtained and demonstrated a large right frontal mass with surrounding edema and approximately 8 mm of leftward midline shift. He was started on levetiracetam and dexamethasone. He has been admitted to the neurosurgery service for further workup and management.
